Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-05-14
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 min
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ben Koh (Redwood SE), Claire Hsu (Bluegrain Platform/SRE), Mateo Alvarez (Bluegrain Infra Eng), Priya Shah (Bluegrain CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Quick status on pilot: latency improvements with new quantization profile, one networking hiccup during last run.
- Plan to upgrade inference kernel on private nodes to 2.1.3; canary + rollback discussed.
- Need firewall IP list, maintenance window, and performance benchmarks before rolling to prod.

Topics: kernel upgrade plan; routing/fallback test results; CVPN/VPC peering; canary strategy; next steps

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this tight, 45 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:05] Claire: Hi, Claire here. Mateo as well.
[00:07] Mateo: Yup.
[00:09] Priya: Priya on this call.
[00:11] Ava: Great. Ben from Redwood is with me — Ben, quick intro?
[00:13] Ben: Hi all, Ben Koh, platform SE. I'll be running the kernel and perf side of the pilot.
[00:17] Ava: Cool. Claire — quick status: how did the last smoke test look outside of the packet drop we saw?
[00:22] Claire: So the smoke was mostly green. We saw the p50 drop from 120ms to ~92ms with the new quantized profile, p95 also improved but p99 still spiky during long seqs, probably KV cache warmups. We also had a firewall rule that killed a node for about 3 minutes, that was operator error on our side, not the provider.
[00:38] Ben: The kernel 2.1.3 has a better attention kernel that reduces softmax overhead for longer contexts. On our infra tests we saw about 8-12% token cost reduction and 10-15% CPU utilization drop. But we need staging perf run with your real seq profile.
[00:52] Mateo: Question — does 2.1.3 change any of the socket/options that your agent uses for keepalive? Because our on-prem firewall is sensitive to long-lived idle TCP connections.
[00:59] Ben: No functional change to keepalive — but scheduling and batching behaviors change timing. We saw more bursty connection patterns, which may trip stateful firewalls if idle timeouts are low.
[01:12] Priya: That's the kind of thing we worry about. We can't have intermittent timeouts during a live run. What's the config knob?
[01:16] Ben: We can switch to smaller continuous batches, or enable connection pooling at the LB layer. Also Redwood's smart router can fallback to a low-batch, low-latency variant when it detects ephemeral failures.
[01:27] Ava: Quick reminder — we have a fallback policy that routes to the hosted fallback pool when packet loss exceeds threshold. Claire, did the fallback fire last week?
[01:34] Claire: It did, once for about 90 seconds during the firewall change. The app saw a brief error and then requests resumed. But we want a cleaner handoff without request failures.
[01:43] Ben: For a cleaner handoff we recommend enabling the graceful drain setting on your LB and increase the detection window to 10s. That avoids mid-request redirects.
[01:51] Mateo: That sounds fine. We'll need the exact IP ranges and ports to allow so the hosted fallback can connect back if needed — can you share those?
[01:58] Ava: Absolutely. I'll drop them after the call. I'll also include the prescriptive firewall rule set in the playbook.
[02:04] Priya: On the canary plan — what are the rollback steps if the kernel causes regressions?
[02:09] Ben: Rollback is straightforward: we maintain the previous runtime image and the KV cache is persisted per-session so we switch image and invalidate cache if needed. We'll keep the rollout small: 2 nodes at a time in cluster-02, monitor 24 hours, then increase.
[02:21] Claire: Will there be any state loss for in-flight sessions? Our UX team needs to know.
[02:25] Ben: In-flight requests will be allowed to finish on the upgraded nodes; we won't drop them. For sessions that rely on local KV cache, those may need a warm restart but we've got a seed-warm option to pre-populate caches.
[02:36] Priya: Okay. On security/compliance: does the upgrade touch our HSM or KMS integrations?
[02:42] Ben: No, KMS/HSM flows are unchanged. We validated the signing of runtime images; it uses the same keychain. We'll provide audit logs for each upgrade action.
[02:51] Mateo: We ran a routing test last night between eu-west and our on-prem DC. We saw 0.4% packet loss for a ten-minute bulk test which is small but might explain spikes. We suspect an edge router queue.
[03:04] Claire: Is that something Redwood can route around?
[03:07] Ben: The smart router can prefer regional egress on a per-customer policy. If we detect degraded path metrics we can route to an alternative egress node in the same region or to the hosted fallback. But it needs metrics from your end as well.
[03:19] Ava: Ben, do we have a telemetry snippet to share that will make it easy for them to correlate with their edge logs?
[03:24] Ben: Yes — a short dashboard and an API query. I'll share a link to the perf CSV and the trace ids for last night's run.
[03:32] Ava: Great. Okay let's go through the canary schedule and the playbook steps quickly.
[03:36] Ben: Step 1: validate firewall rules. Step 2: spin up canary nodes with 2.1.3 on staging using the quantized profile. Step 3: run smoke load for 2h with their seq distribution, capture p50/95/99, token cost. Step 4: if green, schedule on-prem maint window and upgrade 2 nodes in cluster-02, monitor for 24h. Step 5: continue in waves of 4 nodes.
[03:59] Mateo: For step 3 — what's your recommended load generator? We have an internal tool but would prefer a reproducible script.
[04:05] Ben: We'll provide a k6 script with the seq distribution. It maps to the harness we used.
[04:08] Claire: Can we run the script outside peak hours? We'll try to run it tomorrow night.
[04:12] Ben: Sounds good. We'll standby to ingest traces.
[04:15] Priya: If the canary shows a slight p99 regression but cost improved, how do you recommend balancing? We prefer stable latency.
[04:22] Ben: We can tune the quantization profile; there's a middle ground with per-layer rounding that keeps p99 tight while retaining cost benefits. Also routing can degrade to a low-batch variant for latency-sensitive traffic only.
[04:34] Ava: Quick aside — we did a pricing check: dedicated nodes with quantization gave ~22% cost reduction vs stock VM. I will put numbers in the deck.
[04:43] Claire: We need that for procurement approval.
[04:45] Ava: Understood. I'll send the deck and the excel with the unit economics.
[04:49] Ben: One more item: we found a rare segmentation fault in 2.1.3 when sequences exceed 12k tokens on older GPUs. That was in an internal test. We patched it but we'd like to run your long-seq tests on a staging 3090 to be safe.
[05:01] Mateo: We can do that. We'll also add long seq tests to the harness.
[05:05] Priya: Anything else on networking?
[05:07] Claire: We'll provide the firewall list and the router logs. Expect that by Tuesday.
[05:10] Ava: Great. Let's capture the concrete next steps.
